> **Lens**: A plugin's configuration lives where its host keeps configuration; a convention the host's users have never seen needs a stronger reason than convenience.

## Relates to

- Extends [ADR-0023](0023-turn-boundaries-skill-ignore-and-replay.md) (the record's status line says "refines"; its skill-ignore decision)
- Extends [ADR-0014](0014-register-through-the-pytest11-entry-point.md) (the record's status line says "refines")

## Problem

### Symptom

0023 let a skill carry a `.skillignore` at its root, and separately let a project set `xharness_skill_ignore` in its pytest config.
The two lists were concatenated.
In practice the dotfile was the one that got used, because only it could say something about *one* skill.
The ini key had no way to scope a pattern.

### Pain point

A dotfile beside the skill is a new convention with nothing to anchor it.
A pytest user expects a plugin's permanent, file-based configuration in the place pytest keeps its own.
That is `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` in `pyproject.toml`, or `pytest.ini`, `tox.ini` or `setup.cfg`.
Nothing in `pytest --help` or in the project's config hinted that a second file, in a directory pytest never looks in, was also being read.
The skill directory is also shipped to agents as-is.
The dotfile therefore rode along into every `--add-dir` and `$CODEX_HOME/skills` copy.
The agent could see it, and it described a tool the agent had never heard of.
0014 already settled that every location the plugin reads is an ini key resolved against the rootdir; the dotfile was the one exception.

## Decision

### The lens

- **Given**: pytest's own `markers` lines already use a `name: description` form, so a scoped pattern reads as pytest config rather than as a new grammar.
- **We prefer**: `xharness_skill_ignore` as the only source of ignore patterns, over a `.skillignore` dotfile beside the skill or the two concatenated.
- **Because**: A convention the host's users have never seen needs a stronger reason than convenience.
  0014 already settled that every location the plugin reads is an ini key resolved against the rootdir.
- **Unless**: never

### In practice

- `xharness_skill_ignore` is the only source of ignore patterns.
  The `.skillignore` file is not read; a leftover one is just another dotfile, which 0022 never catalogues.
- Each line of the key is either a bare gitignore-style pattern, which applies to every skill, or `<selector>: <pattern>`.
  A selector applies to the skills whose directory name matches it under `fnmatch`.
  `mermaidjs-diagrams: README.md` names one skill, and `*-diagrams: README.md` a family.
  This is the form pytest's own `markers` lines use (`name: description`), so it reads as pytest config rather than as a new grammar.
  A selector with nothing after the colon is a usage error that stops the session at configure time, before any cell is collected.
  It would ignore nothing, and is almost certainly a typo.
  The pattern grammar is unchanged from 0023.

  ```toml
  [tool.pytest.ini_options]
  xharness_skill_ignore = [
      "README.md",                                # every skill
      "mermaidjs-diagrams: resources/examples/**",
      "mermaidjs-diagrams: scripts/{Makefile,CLAUDE.md}",
      "mermaidjs-diagrams: scripts/*.json",
  ]
  ```
- The replay command runs outside a pytest session, so it resolves the key the way pytest would.
  It takes the first ancestor of the captured directory holding a pytest config.
  That is a `pytest.ini`, a `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`, a `tox.ini`, or a `setup.cfg` with a pytest section.
  Its `--ignore` flag takes extra lines in the same form.
  A replay and a live sweep therefore always agree on what is decision surface.

## Consequences

### Pros

- A replay and a live sweep always agree on what is decision surface.

### Cons

- A project that had a `.skillignore` moves its lines into the ini key, prefixed with the skill's name, and deletes the file.
  Until it does, every file of that skill is decision surface again, and `not_loaded` grows.
- Patterns whose path contains `:` cannot be written as bare lines (the first colon is the selector boundary); such files are not portable anyway.
- Skill authors who do not own the project's `pyproject.toml` no longer have a place to declare their skill's edges.
  That is deliberate: which files count is a decision of whoever pays for the sweep.
